caption: A one-way minecart station: the track drops two blocks on two powered rails that slope down the way the carts go. Switched off, a powered rail brakes a cart hard, so every cart coming in, even at full speed, stops on the slope, ridden or empty. The button beside the lower rail (in reach from the cart) switches both rails on: the cart rolls down and is pushed out at speed.

A two-way minecart station: the one-way station's two braking slopes, then a detector rail and an always-on booster. Carts going the station's way stop on the slopes and leave when the button is pressed. Carts coming the other way are sped up by the booster, cross the detector rail quickly, and it switches the slopes on long enough for them to climb straight through.

A hopper-minecart unloader at the end of a line: the cart rolls in over a booster and a detector rail, stops against the end block on a powered rail, and the hopper under that rail empties it into the chest. The powered rail switches on only when the hopper is empty and the detector rail has been quiet for a moment, so a loaded cart waits until its last item has gone and is then pushed back out along the line; an empty cart is sent back at once.

A hopper-minecart loader at the end of a line: boosters send the cart up two slopes to a stop block; it rolls back and halts on the lower slope, a halting powered rail, where the hopper beside it fills it from the chest. A detector rail on the upper slope still sees the parked cart, and its comparator reads how full the cart is. The lower slope switches on, sending the cart back down the line, when every slot is full or when the supply hopper runs empty.

A hopper-minecart unloader at the end of a line: the line comes in one block up and the cart rolls down a detector-rail slope onto a powered rail over a hopper, stopping against the end block; the hopper empties it into the chest. The powered rail switches on only when the hopper is empty and the detector has been quiet for a moment, so a loaded cart waits until its last item has gone and is then pushed back up the line; an empty cart is sent back at once. Gravity on the slope brings even a crawling cart in quickly, so no booster is needed.

A hopper-minecart loader at the end of a line: three boosters (one standing on a redstone block powers them all) send the cart up two slopes to a stop block; it rolls back and halts on the lower slope, a halting powered rail, where the hopper beside it fills it from the chest. A detector rail on the upper slope still sees the parked cart, and its comparator reads how full the cart is. The lower slope switches on, sending the cart back down the line, when every slot is full or when the supply hopper runs empty.
